title: Surface Extraction for Industrial CT Based On Adaptive Particle System
abstract: To achieve high-quality and high-precision surface extraction from industrial CT data, this paper proposes an adaptive surface sampling algorithm based on a particle system. The algorithm first constructs a multi-scale voxel pyramid and performs adaptive subdivision in a coarse-to-fine manner, incorporating curvature information at each scale. The subdivided voxel units serve as the fundamental units for particle behavior. Unlike traditional surface extraction methods based on particle systems, this paper decouples the force mechanism acting on particles in the time domain and adopts an adaptive weighted projection of grayscale and second-order gradient to replace the isosurface gravitational force, driving particles to sample at precise edges. Within the 26-neighborhood of the voxel unit containing the target particle, interacting particles are searched and repulsive forces are calculated to improve computational efficiency. Meanwhile, the tangential component of the repulsive force is extracted to enhance particle distribution while reducing the impact on projection accuracy. Furthermore, to increase sampling density under minimal system energy variation, this paper proposes an incremental particle insertion mechanism based on the Voronoi diagram.\\Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to traditional surface extraction algorithms, the proposed method significantly improves the uniformity of particle distribution and robustness against noise and artifacts while maintaining sampling accuracy. It enables adaptive sampling with fewer sampling points, showing superior engineering practical value in industrial metrological CT applications.
